\textbf{Leave-$k$-out drift of the pooled replication effect.} Points: $\exp$ of the posterior mean of the pooled within-TF log odds ratio $\mu$ of the Bayesian random-effects model, with the exponentiated 95\% credible limits (prior $\mu\sim N(0,1^2)$, $\sigma\sim HN(0.5)$), for the full data and refitted after removing every subset of one (L1O), two (L2O) or three (L3O) units, with studies (a) or cohorts (b) as units; the main text reports the posterior median of $\exp(\mu)$, which is 2.82 at study level against 2.71 for the mean shown here. Open markers: fits that keep a single unit, whose $\mu$ is that unit's effect shrunk towards the prior rather than a pooled estimate. Dashed line: no enrichment; dotted line: full-data posterior mean.
